work-270.rule: We is first and kijken second; uit is separated and the anticipated event follows naar. Uitkijken naar means look forward to. This noun reference uses naar de start, unlike pronominal ernaar uitkijken. Taalcursus is a de-compound; van specifies what starts. The event is still in the future.

examples.dutch: Zij kijkt uit naar haar eerste les.
examples.english: She's looking forward to her first lesson.

examples.dutch: Ik kijk uit naar de vakantie.
examples.english: I'm looking forward to the holiday.

work-271.rule: Ik is first and ben second; the purpose phrase follows hier and ends with te repareren. Om ... te expresses purpose. Lift is a de-word; it is the object within the infinitive phrase. Repareren is not separable, so te stands before the whole verb.

examples.dutch: Ik ben hier om de deur te vervangen.
examples.english: I'm here to replace the door.

examples.dutch: Zij is hier om het apparaat te controleren.
examples.english: She's here to check the device.

work-272.rule: Dit formulier is first and is second. Snel describes completing speed; in te vullen is the final infinitive phrase. Formulier is a het-word and takes dit. Invullen is separable, with te between in and vullen. The construction presents the form as something that can be completed quickly; snel is adverbial here.

examples.dutch: Dit document is snel te lezen.
examples.english: This document can be read quickly.

examples.dutch: Deze doos is snel open te maken.
examples.english: This box can be opened quickly.

work-273.rule: Ze is first and zullen second; te laat precedes infinitive zijn, followed by the registration phrase. Zullen agrees with plural ze. Zijn after the auxiliary is an infinitive. Te is a degree word before laat, not an infinitive marker. The sentence predicts future lateness.

work-274.rule: Ik is first and was second. The toen-clause follows the location and ends with its finite verb aankwam. Toen refers to a particular past moment. Aankomen is separable, but finite aankwam stays whole in this subordinate clause. Op kantoor is a conventional article-free location expression.

examples.dutch: Zij was aanwezig toen de bus aankwam.
examples.english: She was present when the bus arrived.

examples.dutch: Ik werkte toen de telefoon ging.
examples.english: I was working when the phone rang.

work-275.rule: Het is first and is second; beter evaluates the action named by the following infinitive phrase. Beter is comparative better, not superlative best. Het anticipates the action clause. Wachten op is fixed; om ... te names the evaluated action here rather than the purpose of a visit. Bevestiging is a de-word.

examples.dutch: Het is beter om eerst te bellen.
Het is belangrijk om op tijd te komen.
examples.english: It's important to arrive on time.

work-276.rule: Leg begins the instruction and uit ends it; recipient, politeness word and object stand between them. Uitleggen is separable. Inhoud is a de-word; deze agrees with de brief. Me is a recipient object. Alsjeblieft is the informal politeness word, compared with formal alstublieft.

examples.dutch: Leg me alsjeblieft de afspraak uit.
examples.english: Please explain the arrangement to me.

examples.dutch: Leg haar de inhoud van het bericht uit.
examples.english: Explain the content of the message to her.

work-277.rule: Ik is first and ben second. The intended activity follows van plan and ends with te blijven wonen. Van plan zijn takes a te-infinitive, optionally introduced by om. Blijven wonen expresses continued residence; wonen follows blijven without another te. België uses a diaeresis. This is intention, not seeking an opportunity.

examples.dutch: We zijn van plan hier te blijven werken.
examples.english: We're planning to keep working here.

examples.dutch: Zij is van plan in Gent te blijven wonen.
examples.english: She's planning to continue living in Ghent.

work-278.rule: Laten we introduces the shared proposal; the topic over ideas stands before final brainstormen. Brainstormen is commonly used with over for the topic. Ideeën is plural with a diaeresis. Buurtfeest is a compound ending in het feest, indefinite een here. The proposal infinitive has no te.

work-279.rule: Het is first and is second; belangrijk evaluates the following action/state infinitive phrase. Het anticipates the clause describing what is important. Kalm is predicative after blijven and has no -e. Om ... te names the evaluated action; tijdens introduces the time circumstance.

examples.dutch: Het is belangrijk om goed te luisteren.
Het is moeilijk om geduldig te blijven.

work-280.rule: Deze parkeerautomaat is first and is second; gemakkelijk is followed by te gebruiken. Parkeerautomaat is a de-word and takes deze. Gemakkelijk is predicative without -e. The machine is the thing used in the te-infinitive construction, not the person doing the using.

examples.dutch: Dit toestel is gemakkelijk te gebruiken.
examples.english: This device is easy to use.

examples.dutch: Deze sleutel is gemakkelijk te gebruiken.
examples.english: This key is easy to use.

work-281.rule: We is first and moeten second; the object and op elkaar come before final afstemmen. Afstemmen op means to coordinate with. Elkaar is reciprocal: the goals are aligned with each other. Onze agrees with plural doelen. After moeten the separable infinitive stays whole, without te.

examples.dutch: We moeten onze plannen op elkaar afstemmen.
examples.english: We have to coordinate our plans with each other.

examples.dutch: Zij moeten hun werktijden op elkaar afstemmen.
examples.english: They have to coordinate their working hours with each other.

work-282.rule: Hij is first and past-tense voltooide second; the object is followed by the without phrase. Voltooien has regular past voltooide. Zijn is possessive, not a finite verb. Financiële has -e before the de-word steun. Steun is uncountable here. Zonder introduces what was absent.

examples.dutch: Hij voltooide de cursus in juni.
examples.english: He completed the course in June.

examples.dutch: Ik voltooide de oefening zonder hulp.
examples.english: I completed the exercise without help.

work-283.rule: Ik is first and ben second; bang takes its fear object with voor. Bang voor is a fixed adjective-preposition combination. Bang is predicative without -e. Abstract mislukking can refer to failure generally without an article. A particular failed attempt would be een mislukking.

work-284.rule: Dit is first and is second; the challenge phrase is followed by the internship period. Grootste is the superlative of groot, used with -e before uitdaging. Mijn is possessive. Stage means internship or work placement, not an English performance stage. Tijdens takes a noun phrase.

examples.dutch: Dit is onze grootste uitdaging dit jaar.
examples.english: This is our greatest challenge this year.

work-285.rule: We is first and moeten second; the object comes before final aanzetten. Aanzetten is separable: We zetten de verwarming aan. After moeten it remains one infinitive without te. Verwarming is a de-word and here means the heating system.

examples.english: I have to turn on the lamp.
We have to turn on the oven.

work-286.rule: Ik is first and ben second; hier is followed by the om te phrase. Om te blijven expresses intention. Blijven is an infinitive after te. The idiom signals a lasting presence or commitment, rather than only remaining for a few minutes. Hier points to the current workplace.

examples.dutch: Ik ben hier om te helpen.
Zij is hier om te leren.

work-287.rule: We is first and kijken second. The particle uit precedes the naar phrase naming the anticipated reply. Uitkijken naar means to look forward to. Antwoord op introduces what the reply concerns. Onze agrees with the de-word sollicitatie. This present sentence expresses anticipation, not receipt of the answer.

examples.dutch: We kijken uit naar de vakantie.
examples.english: We're looking forward to the holiday.

examples.dutch: Zij kijkt uit naar de uitslag.
examples.english: She's looking forward to the result.

work-288.rule: Zullen is finite in second position, followed by proberen and its complement containing object plus te repareren. Zullen takes proberen without te; proberen takes te repareren. Lek and dak are het-words. The promise concerns an attempt; success is not guaranteed. In het dak specifies the location of the leak.

examples.dutch: Ik zal proberen de deur te repareren.
examples.english: I'll try to repair the door.

examples.dutch: We zullen proberen de fout te vinden.
examples.english: We'll try to find the mistake.

work-289.rule: The formal request begins with fixed Gelieve; uw status precedes the separable te-infinitive bij te werken. Gelieve in this fixed request formula is an old subjunctive form, with understood subject u; it is not the ordinary imperative stem. Uw is formal possessive. Bijwerken is separable, so te goes between bij and werken. This wording is formal and mainly written.

work-290.rule: The imperative Vraag starts the instruction. The short recipient hem comes before the full object phrase. Iemand de weg vragen means to ask someone for directions. Hem is an object pronoun. Weg is a de-word; station is a het-word. Naar introduces the destination.

examples.dutch: Vraag haar de weg naar de bushalte.
examples.english: Ask her for directions to the bus stop.

work-291.rule: Wat is first and zijn second; plural uw verwachtingen is the subject. Verwachtingen is plural, requiring zijn. Uw is formal possessive, not subject u. Wat asks for the content of the expectations. A singular question would be Wat is uw verwachting?

work-292.rule: Zij is first and is second; klaar is followed by an om phrase with object and final toe te lichten. Klaar om expresses readiness for an action. Toelichten is separable, so its te-infinitive is toe te lichten. Haar is possessive with voorstel. Ready does not mean that the explanation has already begun.

examples.dutch: Ik ben klaar om te beginnen.
Zij is klaar om haar plan uit te leggen.
examples.english: She's ready to explain her plan.

work-293.rule: Dit is first and vereist second; the required attention is the object. Vereisen means to require. Vereist is the third-person present. Aandacht is an abstract de-word; attributive onmiddellijke takes -e even without an article in this phrase.

examples.english: This requires a lot of patience.

work-294.rule: The imperative Kom begins the instruction and na closes the separable verb around its object. Nakomen means to fulfil or honour a promise. Je before beloften is possessive, not the subject of a question. Both beloften and beloftes are accepted plurals. The participle is nagekomen.

work-295.rule: Je is first and hebt second; geen verandering stands inside the perfect-tense bracket before aangebracht. Een verandering aanbrengen means to make a change. Geen negates an indefinite noun phrase. Aanbrengen has participle aangebracht: separable aan plus ge plus irregular bracht. Hebben forms the perfect here.

work-296.rule: Wat is first and is second; the subject is followed by the after-interview phrase. Volgende takes -e before de stap. Sollicitatiegesprek is a het-word and takes dit. Mijn is possessive. Stap is figurative for an action in a process.

work-297.rule: Ik is first and doe second; mijn best completes the fixed expression. Je best doen means to make your best effort. Doe is the ik form of doen. Best stays without -e in this expression. The present can describe current effort or a commitment, depending on context.

work-298.rule: Plural Ze is first and waren second; niet negates their being in the room during the conversation. Waren is plural past of zijn. Kamer is a de-word and gesprek a het-word. Tijdens takes a noun phrase. Niet negates the location claim rather than an indefinite object.

examples.dutch: We waren niet op school tijdens de vakantie.
examples.english: We weren't at school during the holiday.

examples.dutch: Zij waren niet in de zaal tijdens de pauze.
examples.english: They weren't in the hall during the break.

work-299.rule: Hij is first and was second; blij takes the reason for satisfaction with met. Was is singular past of zijn. Blij met expresses satisfaction with a result; blij is predicative without -e. Resultaat is a het-word.

examples.dutch: Ik was blij met het cadeau.
examples.english: I was happy with the gift.

examples.dutch: We waren blij met de uitslag.
examples.english: We were happy with the outcome.

work-300.rule: Breng starts the instruction; short recipient me precedes the full object, and terug closes the verb. Terugbrengen is separable. Me is an unstressed object pronoun. Gereedschap is an uncountable het-word for tools collectively. Geleende is an attributive participle with -e after definite het.

examples.dutch: Breng me de geleende boeken terug.
examples.english: Bring the borrowed books back to me.
Bring the key back to her.

work-301.rule: Wat is first and is second; the subject phrase includes an om te explanation of the trick. Truc means a clever method here, not a hidden disadvantage. Knoop is a de-word and takes deze; it means knot in this context. Losmaken is separable: los te maken. The object precedes that infinitive.

examples.dutch: Wat is de truc om dit deksel los te maken?
examples.english: What's the trick to loosening this lid?

examples.dutch: Wat is de truc om deze doos open te maken?
examples.english: What's the trick to opening this box?

work-302.rule: Het is first and is second; tijd is followed by an om phrase with the customers before terug te bellen. Het is tijd om introduces an action that should now begin. Terugbellen is separable and takes te between terug and bellen. Klanten is plural of klant. Het is a dummy subject, not a particular object.

examples.dutch: Het is tijd om de winkel te sluiten.
examples.english: It's time to close the shop.

examples.dutch: Het is tijd om de kinderen op te halen.
examples.english: It's time to pick up the children.

work-303.rule: Hij is first and is second; gewend takes the activity with aan. Gewend aan describes familiarity. Tillen is an infinitive used to name an activity after aan. Zwaar modifies the lifting as an adverb, not an adjective before a noun. This is a present state, not a past habit.

examples.dutch: Ik ben gewend aan vroeg opstaan.
examples.english: I'm used to getting up early.

examples.dutch: Zij is gewend aan lang staan.
examples.english: She's used to standing for a long time.

work-304.rule: Ze is first and plural zijn second; hier gives location and voor names the reason for being there. Plural zijn makes ze mean they. Rondleiding is a de-word and means a guided tour. Voor introduces a noun purpose phrase; it is not the om te construction used before an infinitive.

examples.dutch: We zijn hier voor de tentoonstelling.
Zij zijn hier voor de les.

work-305.rule: Ik is first and denk second; erover anticipates the om te phrase explaining what is being considered. Erover refers to the contemplated action, not a place. Denken over is followed here by om plus object and te starten. Bedrijf is a het-word, but indefinite een does not reveal gender. Thinking about it is not a firm decision.

examples.dutch: Ik denk erover om een cursus te volgen.
examples.english: I'm thinking about taking a course.

examples.dutch: We denken erover om te verhuizen.

work-306.rule: Ik is first and heb second; the object and beneficiary are inside the perfect bracket before gekocht. Kopen has irregular participle gekocht and takes hebben in this perfect. Voor je names the person benefiting. Woordenboek is a compound ending in het boek. Je is an object pronoun after voor.

examples.dutch: Ik heb een plant voor mijn buurvrouw gekocht.
examples.english: I bought a plant for my neighbour.

examples.dutch: Hij heeft een kaart voor zijn broer gekocht.
examples.english: He bought a card for his brother.

work-307.rule: We is first and zitten second; boven ons budget expresses the financial position. Zitten describes being in a situation here, not necessarily physical sitting. Boven means above or beyond the permitted amount. Budget is a het-word, so the possessive is ons, not onze.

examples.dutch: De kosten liggen boven ons budget.
examples.english: The costs are above our budget.

work-308.rule: The full subject Het waterpeil is first and stijgt second. Waterpeil is a compound het-word for water level. Stijgt is the third-person singular present of stijgen. The present can describe a change happening now; Dutch does not require a progressive auxiliary.

work-309.rule: Dat is first and is second; genoeg precedes the uncountable material and voor names its use. Genoeg is a quantity word before verf. Verf is uncountable here, with no indefinite article. Muur is a de-word and takes deze. Dat can refer to the amount of paint just shown.

examples.dutch: Dat is genoeg meel voor het brood.
examples.english: That's enough flour for the bread.

examples.dutch: Dat is genoeg water voor de planten.
examples.english: That's enough water for the plants.

work-310.rule: We is first and plural past verbleven second; the conference period precedes the hotel location here. Verblijven has past singular verbleef and plural verbleven. It means to stay temporarily, not to live permanently. Hotel is a het-word. Tijdens is a preposition before a noun, not a conjunction before a clause.

examples.english: We stayed at a guest house.

work-311.rule: Je is first and hebt second; the negated message and voicemail phrase precede final achtergelaten. Achterlaten is separable; its participle is achtergelaten with ge between achter and laten. Geen negates an indefinite message. Mijn is possessive. Op mijn voicemail specifies where the message would have been left.

work-312.rule: Laat starts the instruction; short recipient ze comes before the full design object, with zien at the end. Laten zien means to show. Zien is a bare infinitive, without te. Ze is an unstressed object pronoun meaning them here. Ontwerp is a het-word; definite het takes attributive nieuwe with -e.

work-313.rule: Ik is first and ga second; the library location stands before final werken. Gaan plus an infinitive can express an intention or upcoming action. Werken stays without te. In de bibliotheek says where the work will happen; it does not say that the speaker works as a librarian.

examples.english: I'm going to study at home.

examples.dutch: We gaan in de tuin eten.
examples.english: We're going to eat in the garden.

work-314.rule: The full subject Onze kookles is first and begint second; nu gives the start time. Kookles is a de-word and takes possessive onze. Begint is third-person singular because lesson is singular, even though onze refers to several people. Nu means now.

work-315.rule: Zij is first and heeft second; paint and beneficiary are before the final participle. Heeft makes zij singular she. Ons is the object pronoun us after voor, not a possessive before verf. Kopen has participle gekocht. Verf is a de-word for paint.

examples.dutch: Zij heeft brood voor ons gekocht.
Hij heeft de kaartjes voor ons gekocht.
examples.english: He bought the tickets for us.

work-316.rule: Laten we introduces a joint proposal; the full decision phrase comes before final nemen. Een beslissing nemen means to make a decision. Over introduces its topic. Vakantiedata is plural of vakantiedatum, with data meaning dates here, not computer information. Nemen is bare after laten.

examples.dutch: Laten we een beslissing over de route nemen.
examples.english: Let's make a decision about the route.

examples.dutch: Laten we een beslissing over het menu nemen.
examples.english: Let's make a decision about the menu.

work-317.rule: Ik is first and heb second; the full requested item stands before nodig. Iets nodig hebben expresses need and is present tense here, not perfect. Met blauwe inkt specifies the pen; blauwe has -e before the de-word inkt. Inkt is uncountable. Nodig is an adjective.

work-318.rule: The yes/no question starts with Zal, followed by je; zijn closes the future bracket before the purpose phrase. Both zal je and zul je are standard. Vrij means available here. Zijn is bare after zal; verhuizen takes te in the separate om phrase. Volgende week needs no preposition.

examples.english: Will you be at home tomorrow?
Will you be available on Sunday?

work-319.rule: The full recipe phrase is first and is second; simpel is the predicate adjective. Recept is a het-word. Soep is a de-word and takes deze. Simpel after is has no attributive -e. Voor deze soep identifies which recipe is meant.

work-320.rule: Laten we introduces the joint proposal; the opportunities phrase precedes final identificeren. Identificeren means to identify or establish which options are available, not yet to choose one. Kansen is plural of kans. Vrijwilligerswerk is an uncountable het-word for volunteer work. No te follows laten.

work-321.rule: Had is second in the main clause and gedaan closes its bracket. Toen introduces a past-event clause with final aankwam. Had plus gedaan is past perfect: completion before another past event. Al means already. Voorbereidende takes -e after definite het werk. Aankomen is separable, but its finite verb stays joined at the end of this subordinate clause.

examples.dutch: Ik had de tafel al gedekt toen de gasten kwamen.
examples.english: I'd already set the table when the guests came.

examples.dutch: We hadden de koffers al gepakt toen de taxi aankwam.
examples.english: We'd already packed the suitcases when the taxi arrived.

work-322.rule: The yes/no question starts with Werk before subject je; nu and the task phrase follow. When subject je or jij follows the finite present verb, werk has no -t. Werken aan names the task being worked on. Verslag is a het-word; van de excursie specifies the report’s topic.

examples.english: Are you working on your homework?
Are you writing a letter now?

work-323.rule: The yes/no question begins with Is; dat is subject and the answer phrase follows. Je is possessive before definitieve antwoord. Definitieve takes -e after a possessive, including with het-word antwoord. Antwoord op names what is answered. Definitief means final rather than provisional.

work-324.rule: Waar is first and is second; zijn kantoor is subject, with the building phrase specifying the search area. Zijn before kantoor is possessive his, not an infinitive. Kantoor and gebouw are het-words; gebouw takes dit. Waar asks for location, not direction.

work-325.rule: The full maintenance phrase is first and is second; belangrijk gives the judgement. Onderhoud is an uncountable het-word. Van deze machine names what is maintained; machine is a de-word. Belangrijk is predicative without -e. This statement evaluates maintenance, rather than issuing a specific obligation.

examples.dutch: Het onderhoud van de fiets is belangrijk.
examples.english: The maintenance of the bicycle is important.

work-326.rule: Ik is first and bel second; the recipient and time phrase come before final terug. Terugbellen is separable. Bel is the ik form. Na mijn werk means after my work period. The present can express a firm near-future intention in this context. Tandarts is a de-word.

examples.dutch: We bellen de garage morgen terug.
examples.english: We'll call the garage back tomorrow.

work-327.rule: We is first and hebben second; the full solution object precedes final gevonden. Vinden has irregular participle gevonden and takes hebben here. Oplossing voor names the problem solved. Opslagprobleem is a compound het-word. The perfect reports a completed discovery, not only the need to find a solution.

examples.dutch: Ik heb een oplossing voor het geluidsprobleem gevonden.
examples.english: I have found a solution to the noise problem.

examples.dutch: Zij hebben een oplossing voor de vertraging gevonden.
examples.english: They have found a solution to the delay.

work-328.rule: Is starts the yes/no question; the shop subject is followed by the Monday phrase and open. Fietsenwinkel is a compound de-word. Open is predicative, with no -e. Op maandag can express a recurring Monday schedule in this opening-hours context; it can also mean a specific Monday in other contexts.

examples.dutch: Is de bakker op zondag open?
examples.english: Is the baker open on Sundays?

examples.dutch: Is de bibliotheek op zaterdag open?
examples.english: Is the library open on Saturdays?

work-329.rule: The company subject is first and heeft second; zijn beleid is inside the perfect bracket before bijgewerkt. Bijwerken is separable and has participle bijgewerkt. Bedrijf and beleid are het-words. Zijn refers possessively to the company, meaning its here; grammatical gender does not make the company a person. Beleid is generally uncountable.

examples.dutch: De school heeft haar regels bijgewerkt.
examples.english: The school has updated its rules.

examples.dutch: De vereniging heeft haar website bijgewerkt.
examples.english: The association has updated its website.

work-330.rule: Two imperatives are joined by en; voordat introduces a clause ending in finite boekt. Wees is the irregular imperative of zijn. Slim is predicative without -e. Vergelijk is the imperative stem of vergelijken. In voordat je boekt, subject je precedes boekt, so its -t stays. Prijzen means monetary prices here.

examples.dutch: Wees voorzichtig en kijk goed voordat je oversteekt.
examples.english: Be careful and look properly before you cross.

examples.dutch: Wees geduldig en wacht totdat je aan de beurt bent.
examples.english: Be patient and wait until it is your turn.
